drones.name: MQ-9 Reaper
drones.blurb: The Air Force's armed surveillance drone, flown over Iran and Yemen throughout the war. Its production line is closed, so every loss comes out of a fleet that can't be refilled quickly.

fleetBefore.by: Air Force budget documents, start of fiscal 2026
fleetBefore.note: Air & Space Forces Magazine reported 182 for the same date; nothing public explains the gap. We use the budget figure.

source.title: USAF Scrambling To Buy What Few MQ-9 Reapers It Can Find After Epic Fury Losses

fleetAfter.by: Lt. Gen. David Tabor, to the Senate Armed Services Committee

source.title: Air Force MQ-9 fleet drops to 135 aircraft after Iran combat losses

losses.by: Pentagon Lead Inspector General, quarterly report to Congress
losses.note: From all causes, February 28 through June 30.

source.title: Iran War Losses: The Pentagon and CBO Finally Publish the Numbers
source.quote: as many as 30 were destroyed in various circumstances through the end of June

losses.by: Three U.S. officials, to the Washington Post
losses.note: From all causes: shoot-downs, crashes, Houthi fire over Yemen and aircraft destroyed on the ground. The Air Force hasn't published its own count. Dated mid-August; the Post's report gives the month only.

source.title: Heavy losses of MQ-9 Reaper to factor in future plans to divest, replace aircraft

drones.name: MQ-1 Gray Eagle
drones.blurb: The Air Force retired its MQ-1 Predators years ago, so an "MQ-1" lost over the Gulf is almost certainly the Army's MQ-1C Gray Eagle. CENTCOM hasn't said which variant.
drones.fleetNote: The Army doesn't publish how many Gray Eagles it has, so there's no stock-left figure, only losses.
